subject: Upgrade threshold, grace period, and rollback scenarios
messages:
From: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@clearsight.health>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Lara Chen <lara.chen@clearsight.health>; legal@clearsight.health
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Upgrade triggers + rollback ask

Kim,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — team was excited about the latency gains. A couple of procurement questions came up from our ops and legal leads that we need to scope before we can sign:

1) Upgrade thresholds: we expect traffic to bump periodically (pilots moving to production). Can we define precise thresholds that auto-trigger an upgrade vs. requiring a manual signed amendment? Our SRE prefers predefined rules rather than ad-hoc calls.

2) Grace period & rollback: if traffic reverts after an upgrade, is there a standard grace period where we can revert to previous plan without penalty, or do we get prorated credits? We need to understand potential overage exposure during the first 60 days after an upgrade.

3) Discount stacking: our finance team asked whether introductory discounts stack with committed capacity discounts for the first year.

Can you share a short customer-facing summary and any internal guidance you need to finalize an amendment? Attachments welcome.

—Tom
Tom Alvarez
Head of Platform Ops
ClearSight Health

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@clearsight.health>
Cc: Lara Chen <lara.chen@clearsight.health>; legal@clearsight.health; Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>; Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Upgrade triggers + rollback ask

Tom — thanks for the clear list. High level summary up front: we can support rule-based upgrades (auto-scale into a higher reserved tier) with a 60-day observational window and a one-time prorated credit if usage falls back below the threshold inside that window. Intro discounts do not stack with committed-capacity discounts; we'll apply the better of the two for the first 12 months.

I'm attaching a draft amendment that captures the mechanics (upgrade triggers, measurement window, rollback credit calc). Internally I'm looping Soojin (pricing) and Priyom (billing) to confirm the exact credit formula and whether we need an exec approval for deeper discounts.

Next steps for us:
- Internal review (Soojin/Priyom): confirm credit math and approval path
- I will share the customer-facing amendment once we have internal alignment
- If that looks good to ClearSight, legal can route an initial signature and we can schedule the tier activation date.

Attachments: upgrade_amendment_draft.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@clearsight.health>, Lara Chen <lara.chen@clearsight.health>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Upgrade triggers + rollback ask — internal pricing check

Kim — quick internal note (keeping the customer looped for transparency):

We can offer the 60-day observational window with the following mechanics:
- Upgrade triggers when a 7-day rolling average tokens/sec exceeds configured threshold X for 3 consecutive days.
- If average usage falls below threshold within 60 days after upgrade, customer receives a prorated credit calculated as (upgrade_cost - baseline_cost) * days_above_threshold / 30, capped at one monthly invoice.
- Introductory promotional discount (10%) applies to the first invoice after upgrade but does not combine with committed-capacity pricing; we will apply whichever results in the lower effective unit price for the first 12 months.

Two internal asks:
1) Do we want to restrict automatic upgrades to customers with committed billing accounts only? (reduces accidental churn)
2) Approval threshold for discounts deeper than 15% — I suggest we route to revenue ops + AE manager.

I've attached a small worksheet with scenario examples.

Attachments: pricing-scenarios-20270601.xlsx (xlsx)

—Soojin
Soojin Lee
Pricing Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@clearsight.health>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Upgrade triggers + rollback ask — billing confirmation

Soojin / Kim — confirmed on billing side: the prorated credit formula looks good but recommend two clarifications for the amendment before customer signature:

1) Define "baseline_cost" as the invoiceable SKU price in the last fully-billed month prior to upgrade activation (explicitly excludes one-off fees).
2) Add a single manual-review escape: if customer workload is seasonal and ops can demonstrate repeated patterns, billing can approve a one-time extended observational window (up to 90 days) but that requires revenue ops sign-off.

Internal note: we should record these rules as a product play in Confluence and tag the amendment number for audit.

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@clearsight.health>
Cc: Lara Chen <lara.chen@clearsight.health>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, legal@clearsight.health
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Upgrade triggers + rollback ask

Tom — thanks for your patience. Summarizing the customer-facing position we can send today (I've kept the language concise for legal):

1) Auto-upgrade trigger: a 7-day rolling average exceeding the agreed threshold for 3 consecutive days will initiate a capacity upgrade to the next reserved tier. Activation date will be scheduled and confirmed in the amendment.

2) Observational window and rollback credit: Redwood will monitor post-upgrade usage for a 60-day observational window. If usage falls back below the agreed threshold during that window, Redwood will apply a prorated credit to your next invoice equal to (upgrade_cost - baseline_cost) * days_above_threshold / 30, capped at one monthly invoice. Customers with documented seasonal patterns may request a one-time extension to 90 days subject to revenue ops approval.

3) Discounts: introductory promotional credit will apply to the first invoice after upgrade; it will not stack with committed-capacity pricing. We will automatically apply the lower effective unit price for the first 12 months. Deeper discounts (>15%) require revenue ops approval.

If that matches ClearSight's expectations, I'll ask legal to incorporate the paragraphs into the amendment and route for signature.

Best,
Kimberly
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: upgrade_amendment_draft.pdf, pricing-scenarios-20270601.xlsx
